transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’ve started to feel like I’m just not good enough at anything anymore, no matter how hard I try. It just feels like I'm constantly falling short lately, and my husband really encouraged me to come in and talk to someone.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life, or did they come on without a clear trigger? About how long have you been feeling this way?

It really started a little over two years ago, and I've felt this way pretty much continuously since then. It began right around the time my husband and I started fertility treatments, which also coincided with me taking on a lot of extra responsibilities at school like mentoring and piloting a new curriculum. I just haven't been able to shake this heavy feeling since all of that piled up.

Do these feelings mostly flare up when you’re dealing with the fertility treatments or work stress, or do they stay present even during calmer periods? Have there been stretches of at least two weeks where you felt down most of the day nearly every day regardless of what was happening?

It stays present all the time, even during calmer periods or when something objectively good happens. I've felt this heavy, low mood nearly every single day for a little over two years now, rather than it just coming and going. It really is like a constant weight that never lifts.

During these past two years, have there been any distinct periods lasting at least 2 months when your mood felt mostly back to normal, or has the depression been continuously present the whole time? Also, were there any stretches of at least 2 weeks when it became clearly worse than your usual baseline with additional symptoms like poor sleep, low energy, appetite change, guilt, or trouble concentrating?

No, I haven't had any breaks or periods of feeling normal at all over these past two years; it has been completely continuous. It has felt like a steady, constant weight rather than coming in distinct, sudden waves, though the overall exhaustion and feeling of failure have gradually worn me down to this point.

Along with this persistent low mood, have you also had at least two of these most days for the past two years: low energy, poor self-esteem, trouble concentrating or making decisions, poor appetite or overeating, trouble sleeping or sleeping too much, or feeling hopeless? Have there ever been times when these symptoms became much more severe for at least two weeks?

Yes, I've definitely struggled with several of those, especially feeling constantly exhausted, having terrible self-esteem where I feel like a bad wife and a mediocre teacher, and feeling completely hopeless about the future. It hasn't really spiked in distinct, extra-severe two-week periods, though; it has just been a steady, heavy, low-grade feeling dragging me down continuously the entire time.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a chronically depressed mood present nearly every day for over 2 years, without remission periods of 2 months or more, along with low energy, poor self-esteem, and hopelessness. There were no distinct superimposed major depressive episodes described. This pattern is most consistent with persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia).
